trial_name.text: Study 1053 (CD-ON-CAT-8015-1053), "A Pivotal Multicenter Trial of Moxetumomab Pasudotox in Relapsed/Refractory Hairy Cell Leukemia"

citations.quote: The efficacy of LUMOXITI was based upon Study 1053 titled “A Pivotal Multicenter Trial of Moxetumomab Pasudotox in Relapsed/Refractory Hairy Cell Leukemia” (NCT01829711).
One clinical site (Dr. Wyndham Wilson) was selected by the Division of Hematology Products for inspection of study conduct for Study CD-ON-CAT-8015-1053, submitted in support of BLA 761104.

Study 1053 was an open-label single-arm multicenter clinical trial of moxetumomab pasudotox which enrolled adults with relapsed or refractory HCL.

population.text: Adults with relapsed or refractory HCL who had received at least 2 prior systemic therapies including a purine nucleoside analog (PNA); heavily pretreated, median 3 prior therapies (range 2-11), median age 60 years

citations.quote: Study 1053 was an open-label single-arm multicenter clinical trial of moxetumomab pasudotox which enrolled adults with relapsed or refractory HCL. The median age was 60 years (range: 34-84) and the median number of prior therapies was 3 (range: 2-11).
who had received prior treatment with at least 2 systemic therapies, including 1 purine nucleoside analog (PNA).

endpoint.text: Rate of durable complete response (CR) per blinded independent central review (BICR), defined as CR followed by hematologic remission maintained for more than 180 days

citations.quote: The primary endpoint was rate of durable CR based on CR as determined by blinded independent central review (BICR). Durable CR was defined as the overall response that meets blood, bone marrow, and imaging criteria for CR per BICR, followed by hematologic remission with duration of > 180 days, with hematologic remission defined as the blood counts needed for CR.
A total of 80 patients were enrolled; 77 with classic HCL and 3 with HCL variant.

result.text: IRC-assessed durable CR rate 30% (24/80; 95% CI: 20, 41); ORR 75% (95% CI: 64, 84); CR 41% (95% CI: 30, 53); median duration of response not reached

indication.text: Treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory hairy cell leukemia (HCL) who received at least two prior systemic therapies, including treatment with a purine nucleoside analog (PNA)

citations.quote: LUMOXITI is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory hairy cell leukemia (HCL) who received at least two prior systemic therapies, including treatment with a purine nucleoside analog (PNA).

target_moa.text: CD22-directed cytotoxin: an anti-CD22 antibody fragment fused to truncated Pseudomonas exotoxin PE38; binds CD22 on B cells, is internalized, and causes ADP-ribosylation of eukaryotic elongation factor 2, inhibiting protein synthesis and causing apoptotic cell death

citations.quote: Moxetumomab pasudotox (approximately 63 kDa) is composed of an immunoglobulin light chain variable domain (VL) and a heavy chain variable domain (VH) genetically fused to a truncated form of *Pseudomonas* exotoxin, PE38.

Moxetumomab pasudotox binds CD22 on the cell surface of B cells and is internalized. Moxetumomab pasudotox internalization results in ADP-ribosylation of eukaryotic elongation factor 2, inhibition of protein synthesis, and apoptotic cell death.

modality.text: Immunotoxin (recombinant CD22-directed antibody-fragment/Pseudomonas exotoxin fusion cytotoxin) — other

citations.quote: LUMOXITI is a CD22-directed cytotoxin indicated for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory hairy cell leukemia (HCL) who received at least two prior systemic therapies, including treatment with a purine nucleoside analog (PNA). (1)

key_safety.text: Most common (≥20%) non-laboratory adverse reactions: infusion related reactions, edema, nausea, fatigue, headache, pyrexia, constipation, anemia, diarrhea. Boxed warning toxicities: capillary leak syndrome (CLS) in 34% (44/129) and hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) in 7% (9/129). Discontinuations for AEs in 15% (12/80), most commonly HUS (5%).

citations.quote: The most common non-laboratory adverse reactions (\ge 20\%) of any grade were infusion related reactions, edema, nausea, fatigue, headache, pyrexia, constipation, anemia, and diarrhea.

In the combined safety database of HCL patients treated with LUMOXITI, HUS occurred in 7% (9/129) of patients, including Grade 3 in 3% (4/129) and Grade 4 in 0.
Adverse reactions resulting in permanent discontinuation of LUMOXITI occurred in 15% (12/80) of patients. The most common adverse reaction leading to LUMOXITI discontinuation was HUS (5%).

detail.text: Boxed warning for Capillary Leak Syndrome (CLS) and Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS), including life-threatening cases; delay dosing or discontinue as recommended, and discontinue LUMOXITI in patients with HUS

citations.quote: ## WARNING: CAPILLARY LEAK SYNDROME AND HEMOLYTIC UREMIC SYNDROME

- Capillary Leak Syndrome (CLS), including life-threatening cases, occurred in patients receiving LUMOXITI. Delay dosing or discontinue LUMOXITI as recommended. (2.3, 5.1)
- Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS), including life-threatening cases, occurred in patients receiving LUMOXITI. Discontinue LUMOXITI in patients with HUS. (2.3, 5.2)
